standard_prerequisites: The descent tower situation with its system of objects and the object K defined as the derived limit of the system, and the identification of RHom with RGamma composed with the internal Hom sheaf
The base change lemma for RHom against a perfect object: the stages RHom_{X_n}(E_n, F_n) are perfect over A_n with formation commuting with base change
The More on Algebra lemma that a derived limit of perfect objects with compatible base change data is perfect and recovers the stages on base change
The duality between derived global sections and derived hom translating tensor statements into hom statements for perfect objects
core_obligations: Identify RHom with RGamma of the internal Hom sheaf, so that the base change lemma for RHom against a perfect object makes N_n = RHom_{X_n}(E_n, F_n) a perfect object of D(A_n) whose formation commutes with base change, whence the transition maps N_n tensor A_{n-1} -> N_{n-1} are isomorphisms
The More on Algebra limit lemma makes N = R lim N_n a perfect object of D(A) whose base change to A_n recovers N_n

The exact functor RHom_X(E, -) commutes with products and hence with derived limits, giving the chain RHom_X(E, K) = R lim RHom_X(E, F_n) = R lim RHom_X(E_n, F_n) = R lim N_n = N, which proves part two
Part one follows by translating it into part two with the duality lemma for perfect complexes
proof_roadmap: Prove the RHom statement first: perfectness of the stages with base change compatible transitions, then the limit lemma, then commutation of RHom with derived limits
Chain the identifications RHom(E, K) = R lim RHom(E, F_n) = R lim N_n
Derive the tensor statement from the hom statement by the perfect duality lemma
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the two perfectness-and-base-change assertions for M = RGamma(X, K tensor E) and N = RHom_X(E, K) at source lines 2404-2422, label lemma-compute-against-perfect, whose proof occupies source lines 2424-2452. The proof is not a bare citation chain: it sets up the stages N_n, derives their base change compatible perfectness, produces the limit object N = R lim N_n with recovery isomorphisms, and carries out the commutation argument that RHom_X(E, -) commutes with products and hence with derived limits, chaining it against the definition of K as the derived limit; part one is then obtained by an explicit duality translation. The counted statement records none of this: neither the stage-wise setup nor the limit commutation nor the duality reduction appears in it.
